investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only (SUFFICIENT) — no browser/headless session at any point. All retained evidence acquired via plain curl (raw HTTP GET, and one plain HTTP POST submitting exactly the field names/values a retained public HTML <form> itself declares — no JS execution, no session/login, no private endpoint), real descriptive User-Agent (BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1). This investigation started from sources/porto.json's existing 'cm-matosinhos-agenda-cultural-amp' entry (events_url https://www.cm-matosinhos.pt/servicos/cultura/agenda-cultural-da-amp) and found that URL is NOT itself an events listing at all — it is a static informational article page (data-content_type=Article) describing 'iPorto', an Área Metropolitana do Porto (AMP) initiative covering 16 municipalities, and pointing readers to a THIRD-PARTY domain, iporto.amp.pt, for the actual programme. This investigation independently probed iporto.amp.pt (a WordPress site with a public /wp-json/wp/v2/event REST API, a 'counties' taxonomy including Matosinhos, and a 'categories' taxonomy including Música) far enough to confirm the naming-caution in this task's brief is real (that portal genuinely aggregates 16 municipalities, and its own Matosinhos-tagged content is filed by an AMP-operated third party, not CM Matosinhos itself) — then went further and found the decisive clue on one of that portal's own event pages: a 'Mais informação' link back to https://www.cm-matosinhos.pt/evento/{slug}. Following that link proved CM Matosinhos' OWN domain independently hosts a genuine, first-party, native event-detail template (an 'EventDetail' widget) for the very same events, with structured add-to-calendar (atc_date_start/atc_date_end/atc_timezone) fields, a native category taxonomy including 'Eventos | Música', and a native venue/location taxonomy of exclusively Matosinhos venues. From there this investigation located CM Matosinhos' own native, category-filtered, paginated, plain-GET events listing at https://www.cm-matosinhos.pt/servicos/comunicacao-e-imagem/eventos/musica (an 'EventsList' widget, page 1 of 31, ?events_list_64_page=N pagination) — the genuine, recommended acquisition path, wholly independent of the registry's given (dead-end) events_url and of the third-party AMP portal. A public 'EventSearchForm' widget (category_id=34 = 'Eventos | Música') was also read directly from its own retained HTML and submitted via a plain POST as a bounded, confirmatory cross-check (not the recommended mechanism) — including once with its own start_date filter to bound a genuine current/future count. Level 1 answered every question this investigation needed; no Level 2/3/4 escalation was attempted or needed.

probe_history.reason: A plain, unauthenticated GET of the registry's given events_url (https://www.cm-matosinhos.pt/servicos/cultura/agenda-cultural-da-amp) already exposed everything needed to classify it: a fully server-rendered, static informational Article widget with no event data of its own, explicitly stating the 'Agenda Cultural da AMP' ('iporto') is a Junta Metropolitana do Porto initiative covering 16 AMP municipalities, published quarterly, and directing readers to a separate domain (http://iporto.amp.pt) for the actual programme. Following that same plain-GET discipline to iporto.amp.pt (still a plain, unauthenticated request) exposed a WordPress 'Link' response header pointing at /wp-json/ and, from there, a public /wp-json/wp/v2/event REST route with 'categories' (Música, id 36) and 'counties' (Matosinhos, id 45) taxonomies filterable via plain query-string GET — all discoverable without any JS execution, login, or browser session. One sampled iporto.amp.pt event's own server-rendered HTML detail page (still a plain GET) then contained a 'Mais informação' link back to CM Matosinhos' own domain (https://www.cm-matosinhos.pt/evento/{slug}) — following that link (again a plain GET) revealed CM Matosinhos' own native, first-party 'EventDetail' widget with structured add-to-calendar microformat fields (atc_date_start/atc_date_end/atc_timezone), a native category taxonomy including 'Eventos | Música', and a native, Matosinhos-only venue/location taxonomy. From CM Matosinhos' own /agenda and /servicos/comunicacao-e-imagem/eventos pages (both plain GETs) this investigation then found a public 'EventSearchForm' widget (its own HTML directly names category_id=34 as 'Eventos | Música') and, from the site's own left-nav, a clean, bookmarkable, plain-GET, paginated URL already scoped to that same category: https://www.cm-matosinhos.pt/servicos/comunicacao-e-imagem/eventos/musica. Every one of these steps — reading server-rendered HTML, a WP REST Link header, a public HTML <form>'s own field names, and a site's own left-nav links — is squarely Level 1 (plain response bodies, headers, links, static event cards, known-platform fingerprints); no JS bundle was inspected, no headless/browser session was opened, and no private/undocumented endpoint was used. This single Level 1 pass fully answered identity, platform classification, data-path discovery, the naming-caution question (which events are genuinely IN Matosinhos), and field assessment, so no escalation to Level 2/3/4 was needed or attempted.

site_classification.platform: A shared Portuguese municipal-government website platform (CSP 'frame-ancestors *.skillmind.pt' on every page; asset paths under /assets/wm-smile/ and /assets/wm-citizen/; widgets self-identify via data-content_type attributes: Article, EventsList, EventDetail, EventSearchForm, HorizontalMenu, VerticalMenu, Breadcrumb, SiteMap, HtmlBlock). The site's own left-hand category nav additionally exposes a clean, bookmarkable, plain-GET URL per category (e.g. /servicos/comunicacao-e-imagem/eventos/musica), paginated via a plain ?events_list_64_page=N query parameter — no POST/session/CSRF token required to read it.
